title: lumbr — the alert → investigate → fix loop, closed
asOf: As of 2026-09-02 · authored from the repo (7 packages, 16k lines) · consumer #2

intro.title: Agents that read the telemetry and are allowed to act
intro.sub: the observability space stops at suggest — lumbr closes the loop under policy
intro.proseHTML:
What this is

Agents with situational awareness (read) plus execution capability (write). Humans set policy; agents handle the rest. The read layer is an OpenTelemetry pipeline with a wide-event schema; the referee is an MCP server any agent can load; the write layer executes four safe remediations behind a policy gate, a confidence scorer, and a trust ledger that humans can audit.

This map is isoscope's second real consumer: authored from lumbr's package graph, its uncommitted working tree, and its planning ledger — so the open items are real. Press Stack to separate read, referee, and write.

nodes.name: Instrumentation SDK
nodes.does: What a service calls to be seen: initLumbr() wires an OTel tracer, the LumbrSpanProcessor injects session identity from baggage, and a token-velocity exporter turns LLM spans into the signals the referee watches.
nodes.built: OTLP trace export (Honeycomb-shaped), a demo harness, ~900 lines. Runs under doppler for credentials.

nodes.name: Wide-event schema
nodes.does: The contract every span must meet: twelve required fields per wide event, extending the OTel GenAI semantic conventions (opt-in, pinned). session_id rides in baggage — it is not native OTel.
nodes.built: Types + validators, ~500 lines. Imported by the referee to check what it reads.

nodes.name: Observability backends
nodes.does: Where the wide events live: Honeycomb for traces, SurrealDB for lumbr's own stores (policy versions, evaluations, trust ledger). The referee reads through a backend interface so either can answer.
nodes.built: Two backend adapters inside the MCP server; SurrealDB via docker-compose locally. Param-binding hardened in EPIC-9 (E9S1–S3).

nodes.name: MCP observability server
nodes.does: The tool surface any agent loads: four observability signals (error-rate acceleration, tool-call failure acceleration, token-velocity decline, output-length collapse), plus policy, execution, and trust-export tools. Everything an agent needs to notice, decide, and act — through one stdio JSON-RPC door.
nodes.built: ~3.3k lines; tools split by domain; stderr-only logging keeps stdout clean for the protocol. Phase-1 GTM distribution surface (EPIC-1).

nodes.name: Remote MCP worker
nodes.does: The same server, hosted: a Cloudflare Worker wraps createLumbrMcpServer() in a stateless Streamable-HTTP handler behind a timing-safe bearer token. POST /mcp for tools, GET /healthz for liveness.
nodes.built: ~200 lines, Agents SDK handler, no Durable Objects. Private — never published to npm.

nodes.name: Policy engine
nodes.does: Humans write the rules; this enforces them. Policy schema + validation, a versioned SurrealDB store, a confidence scorer (determinism, pattern confidence, recency, ambiguity penalty), a rate limiter, and the blast-radius evaluator that decides how much an action may touch.
nodes.built: ~3.4k lines. Four starter rules ship: pod restart, deployment rollback, cache clear, cert renewal. The PolicyGate contract lives in execution (dependency inversion) — this package implements it.

nodes.name: Execution substrate
nodes.does: The write layer: a RunbookExecutor with preflight checks, trigger evaluators (error rate, OOMKill, cache health, cert expiry), providers for Kubernetes, Redis and cert-manager, verification after the act, and an immutable audit store of every step taken.
nodes.built: ~4.5k lines. Level-2 beachhead: four safe remediations end-to-end (EPIC-2/3). Webhook entry for external triggers.

nodes.name: Trust & audit layer
nodes.does: Why an operator can let this run: an accuracy scorer per remediation, a state machine for trust levels, an exception router that escalates the unusual, notification channels (Slack live; PagerDuty and email stubbed), SRE feedback intake, and an audit exporter.
nodes.built: ~3.3k lines. Dashboard aggregates the ledger. EPIC-4.

nodes.name: Remediation targets
nodes.does: What the write layer is allowed to touch: Kubernetes workloads (restart, rollback), Redis caches (clear), cert-manager certificates (renew). Each behind its provider interface, each with a preflight and a verify.
nodes.built: Provider interface + three providers; the Kubernetes provider is the beachhead, the others follow the same shape.

nodes.name: Planning & governance
nodes.does: How the repo is allowed to change: epics → stories → DEV/QA slice pairs with holdouts, dispatch ledgers, escalations, and an auto-generated status board. Every package above landed through this loop.
nodes.built: planning/ tree + .claude/hooks that enforce slice pairing, immutable ids, and post-push CI verification. 76/76 slices in done/.

IN-BK.title: Spans out
IN-BK.carries: OTLP traces with lumbr's wide-event attributes and baggage-propagated session_id, exported to Honeycomb.

IN-SC.title: Conformance, not import
IN-SC.carries: Every span the SDK emits is meant to satisfy the twelve-field schema; nothing enforces it at emit time yet — the referee validates on read.

BK-MS.title: The referee reads
BK-MS.carries: Queries over traces and lumbr stores: error rates, tool-call failures, token velocity, output lengths — the raw material of the four signals.

SC-MS.title: Validate what you read
SC-MS.carries: Schema types and validators applied to backend rows before a signal is computed.

MW-MS.title: Hosted door
MW-MS.carries: Authenticated JSON-RPC over Streamable HTTP — a fresh server per request, identical tool names to the stdio CLI.

MS-PO.title: May I?
MS-PO.carries: Proposed actions submitted to the policy gate; back come a verdict, a confidence score, and the blast-radius level.

MS-EX.title: Do it
MS-EX.carries: Runbook execution requests with the policy verdict attached; execution replies with preflight, steps, verify, and the audit id.

MS-TR.title: Tell the humans
MS-TR.carries: Trust-level reads, exception routing, and audit export for the operator's dashboard.

PO-EX.title: The gate is a contract
PO-EX.carries: PolicyGate / PolicyGateResult are declared in execution and implemented in policy — the write layer never imports the rules, the rules plug into it.

TR-EX.title: Every act is scored
TR-EX.carries: Audit records and outcomes flow into accuracy scoring and the trust state machine.

EX-TG.title: Hands on the system
EX-TG.carries: Provider calls: restart / rollback a workload, clear a cache, renew a certificate — each after preflight, each verified after.

PL-MS.title: Under governance
PL-MS.carries: Nothing ships without a DEV/QA slice pair and a holdout; the referee is the most-shipped surface and the hooks guard it.

traceText.IN-BK: A service is instrumented; its spans, tagged with session identity, land in the backend.
traceText.BK-MS: The referee reads them and computes its four signals.
traceText.SC-MS: Only rows that satisfy the wide-event schema count.
traceText.MS-PO: A signal crosses a threshold; the agent asks policy whether the fix is allowed.
traceText.PO-EX: The gate answers through a contract the write layer owns.
traceText.MS-EX: Permission in hand, the agent executes the runbook.
traceText.EX-TG: The provider acts on the real system — after preflight, before verify.
traceText.TR-EX: The audit record is scored; trust moves.
traceText.MS-TR: Humans see it: dashboard, exceptions, notifications. The loop is closed.
